body:
Merged `main` (a2f8218b3) into the branch to remove the conflict with #4192. New head: 1a734add8 (merge commit, no rebase, no force-push).

Resolution, for each file:
- `crates/tools/src/lib.rs`: both sides added module lines at the same place. I kept the two sides: `lathe_assembly` (#3643) and `milling_cutter` (#3646).
- All other files merged without a conflict.

Adapted calls: none. `crates/tools/src/milling_cutter_assembly.rs` (#4192) calls `tool_assembly::resolve`. This PR moves the start of `resolve` into `pub(crate) fn placed`, and `resolve` calls it. The signature, the checks and the result of `resolve` do not change. Thus the call of #4192 needs no change.

`git diff origin/main --stat` shows only the files of this PR.

Gate on 1a734add8 (Windows build lane, log head `1a734add82e928702d68fd95d3676a02927d2744`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 2 steps, 0 failed (`tools suites: lib`, `app suites: turning_insert_zone`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib`: `lathe_assembly` 7 passed, `milling_cutter` 10 passed, `tool_assembly` 11 passed.

Ready for review.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This PR is a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut.

Review tier: SAFETY. The `LatheClearance` bands that this PR makes are the input of the lathe collision checks. Thus I ran mutations myself. The PR changes no posted G-code, no golden and no stock simulation.

## What looks good

- The resolver is pure domain code in `camcraft-tools`. It adds no crate edge, no ECS code and no file I/O. The `use` lines name only `camcraft-tools` modules.
- `tool_assembly::placed` is an exact move of the first steps of `resolve`. The checks, the order and the result of `resolve` do not change. The 11 spindle tests and the 10 `milling_cutter` tests stay green.
- Each failure path returns a named `LatheAssemblyError`. There is no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` outside the tests. The indexes `nodes[cut]` come from `placed`, which checks them.
- The nose-centre formula agrees with `orientation::tip_offset`. For orientation 2, the CRP is at `(-r, 0, -r)` from the nose centre, and the edge check refuses a body point with `-x > r` or `-z > r`. The sign is correct for all eight codes.
- The edge check is linear on the clipped polygon. Thus a test of the polygon corners is a test of the full clipped facet.
- A revolved body on a lathe component is refused by name. It is never dropped. The insert plate is left out of the bands, as the decision says.
- Each new file has a provenance line. The files have 306, 82 and 326 lines (all below 400). `tool_assembly.rs` has 355 lines.
- The decision entry in `docs/decisions/3643-tool-assemblies.md` gives what was chosen, why, and what was dropped.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Refs #3643` (partial work). The commit subjects are conventional.

## Mutations (run by the reviewer)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| The nose-centre shift has the wrong sign (`c - r*...` to `c + r*...`) | RED: 5 tests |
| The edge check is off (`if false && ...`) | RED: the wrong-hand test and the 180-degree bar test |
| The window test reads only the facet corners, not the clipped polygon | GREEN: 7 passed |

## Requested before merge

None.

## Optional, non-blocking

1. The PR body says: "The window is clipped exactly, so a large facet with its corners outside the window is checked too." No test pins this. The third mutation above stays green. The code is correct, but a future change can lose the clip and no test will fail. Recommended follow-up (P7): add a refusal test with a wrong-hand body box that is larger than the window (each corner more than 25.4 mm from the nose), so that only the clip can find the overlap.
2. `resolve_lathe` calls `placement.basis()` two times (first on `axes`, then on `placement`). The second call only adds the tip check. This is correct. A comment can say why the second call is necessary.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
